comment: The foundational-DPI assessment asks about identity, payments, and data exchange but omits potentially relevant capabilities such as trust services, digital signatures, organisational identity, geospatial infrastructure, civil registration, consent, notifications, and public-sector cloud.

public.text: The foundational-DPI assessment asks about identity, payments, and data exchange but omits potentially relevant capabilities such as trust services, digital signatures, organisational identity, geospatial infrastructure, civil registration, consent, notifications, and public-sector cloud.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that identity, payments, and exchange are the principal DPI-F areas considered, while countries should assess any additional shared national capabilities relevant to health.
